text: This is a housekeeping step rather than a new capability: it simplifies the Rust port's internals and adds a plain record of what has been merged, so the port stays easy to follow as it grows one tested step at a time. That matters because the whole method depends on each step being understandable and checkable against the C++ original, and a tidy, documented codebase keeps that comparison honest. The scoreboard shows why the work continues: xs-rs is already faster on the sample collections, finishing in roughly 86–95% of the C++ time across fresh, no-op and partial-update runs, but on the real-projects collection it is still slower, at about 1.46 times the C++ time for a fresh copy and 1.66 times for a no-op run.
